match.reason: None of the bank points teaches the social model of health as a concept. The closest, social justice in health and health promotion, are related but cover equity principles and intervention types rather than this model of health's causes, so a new point is needed.

draft.title: The social model of health
card: The social model of health looks at the causes behind illness, not only the illness itself. These include social, economic and environmental conditions.
Examples are income, education, employment, housing and access to services. These shape who is healthy and who is not.
The model involves communities in making decisions about their own health. It also aims to reduce inequity, which means unfair differences in health between groups.
It looks at the whole population and aims to prevent illness. This differs from an approach that mainly treats people once they are sick.
draft.remember: The social model asks why people get sick and acts on those causes, with communities, to make health fairer.

a.q: Which action best reflects the social model of health?
opts: Improving housing and job access in a low-income suburb
Opening a new hospital ward for heart surgery
Buying scanning machines for a city clinic
Hiring more specialist doctors to treat illness
a.why: Housing and jobs are social and economic causes of health, and fixing them can reduce inequity. The other options focus on treating people once they are already sick, which is not the aim of the social model.
a.clue: Which option acts on the conditions that cause illness?

b.q: A council in regional Victoria finds that residents in one town have poorer health than those in a nearby town. It asks residents what they need, then funds local transport and a community garden. Why does this fit the social model?
opts: It involves residents and tackles causes of unequal health
It treats illness quickly using doctors and medicine
It relies on experts alone to decide what the town needs
It targets only the health of people who are already sick
b.why: The council involves residents in decisions and acts on social and environmental conditions to reduce the health gap between towns. Treating illness with doctors and medicine is a different approach, and the council is not doing it here.
b.clue: Look at who made the decisions and what the funding was aimed at.

a.best: Improving housing and job access in a low-income suburb

b.best: It involves residents and tackles causes of unequal health

problems.detail: The right option is the only one without an absolute qualifier: the distractors say "only" and "alone". It also echoes the stem, which asks residents and says one town has poorer health. A student could pick it by test-taking cues without knowing the model.
